items.summary: Eight Instagram posts in 48 hours. For independent journalist and educator Raghav Trivedi, who has 772,000 followers, the takedowns came in quick succession, leaving him questioning why his content was being removed. “I have had eight videos taken down. Whenever I upload a video, it gets blocked in India within 30 to 35 minutes. I uploaded six videos yesterday and tried uploading two more, but those were blocked as well,” Trivedi told Newslaundry . He is among several independent journalists, content creators and media organisations who have reported their posts being taken down and accounts restricted on Meta platforms, often without a clear explanation. In this report, a post described as “restricted” or “blocked in India” cannot be viewed by users in India. Data compiled by the Software Freedom Law Centre (SFLC.in) records 268 instances of content restrictions and 83 instances of account restrictions across Meta platforms, X, Reddit and YouTube in October. items.title: People’s tribunal indicts Delhi Police over handling of July protest
items.summary: A report by a people’s tribunal has concluded that the Delhi Police and paramilitary forces used force that was neither necessary nor proportionate against the July 20 student march to Parliament. The Constitutional Conduct Group, an informal collective of former bureaucrats, released the report at the Press Club of India on Friday. The report argues that the state treated a constitutionally protected assembly as a threat to pre-empt, skipping the dialogue, warning and graded force that law and police orders require. It also warns that the pattern is repeating, citing reported detentions during the October anti-SIR protests, and says the law on protest policing, not just individual officers, needs to change. The tribunal was chaired by Justice Anjana Prakash, a senior advocate and former Patna High Court judge. Its members were former Union Home Secretary Gopal Krishna Pillai, former civil servant Aditi Mehta, former National Judicial Academy director Mohan Gopal, academic Radha Kumar and historian Tanika Sarkar. Harsh Mander convened it. The tribunal heard 25 people, including injured protesters, lawyers, doctors, journalists and retired police officers. The Delhi Police and the Rapid Action Force were invited but did not respond. “Ultimately, the events examined in this report raise a fundamental question for Indian democracy: whether the State will treat peaceful protest as a constitutionally protected form of public participation or increasingly approach dissent as a threat to be suppressed. The protection of democratic rights requires more than the formal recognition of constitutional freedoms. It requires law enforcement agencies to respect those freedoms in practice, to exercise coercive powers within clearly defined legal limits, and to ensure that violations are investigated transparently and remedied effectively. Democratic policing must preserve public order without extinguishing the right to dissent,” it notes. The report explored several broad questions before arriving at its conclusions with testimonies. Did the police leadership attempt to negotiate with the leaders of the protesters before the protests or before the actual use of force? items.title: 'Targeted for raising our voice': SRFTI students' union VP booked for alleged assault
items.summary: The Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute (SRFTI) in Kolkata has filed a case against students’ union vice president Shubham Waydande for allegedly assaulting its vice chancellor. Waydande is one of six students the institute rusticated on October 15. He was rusticated for three semesters, while the other five were rusticated for two semesters each. The campus has remained tense for the past month. It all began on September 27, when students protested an event on campus organised by the Akhil Bharatiya Grahak Panchayat, a body affiliated with the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh. Students and organisers clashed. On October 4, a large crowd from outside gathered at the institute’s gate and shouted slogans. There were also reports of stone-pelting and injured students. SRFTI clarifies that disciplinary action against certain students stems from specific acts of misconduct, including vandalism, defacement, and physical assault—not peaceful protest. The Institute upholds the right to peaceful dissent while ensuring accountability under its rules.… pic.twitter.com/6SG9VarOj0 — Satyajit Ray Film & Television Institute (@srfti_official) October 25, 2026 Students are still protesting, demanding campus security and administrative accountability. The police presence on campus has also drawn questions. Waydande has been booked under Sections 126(2), 115(2), 121(1), 221, 351(2), 352, 324(4), 3(5) and 54 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Waydande told Newslaundry that he and a few other students were holding a peaceful protest outside the vice chancellor’s office on October 15. The vice chancellor, he said, was already surrounded by security personnel. As far as he knows, someone threw a stone at a window, but he does not know who. The next day, the vice chancellor said the office had been vandalised and announced that CCTV cameras would be installed. Six students were rusticated. According to Waydande, the students asked the vice-chancellor why the administrative gates were closed, why students were not being given access to facilities, and why rusticated students were not being allowed to meet the registrar. On the FIR, Waydande said: “I have come here to learn filmmaking, but raising questions and protesting against wrongdoing is also my right. items.summary: ​Having successfully imported the grand scale of the North Indian Kumbh Mela to the banks of the Bharathapuzha in Malappuram district, the organisers of Kerala’s ‘Maha Magha Mahotsavam’ are now split. Festival committees of Thavanur and Thirunavaya, representing two banks of the river Bharathapuzha, who had been organising the event since 2016 and Varanasi’s Sri Panch Dasnam Juna Akhada, who made their entry in 2025 assuming a leadership role, are now locked in a bitter feud. The rift has been caused by concerns regarding financial transparency, and allegations of one-upmanship and sidelining of Kerala-based sanyasins against Juna Akhada’s Maha Mandaleshwar Swami Anandavanam Bharati. Mahamandaleshwar Swami Anandavanam Bharati In 2025, Anandavanam Bharati, the oldest and the most influential Shaivite monastic order from North India, which plays a significant role in Kumbh Mela, took over the chairmanship of the event. With Anandavanam Bharati declaring a 51-day event from January 15, 2027 and the local committees, which has allegiance with Swami Chidanandapuri vowing to run their own, Kerala is likely to witness two competing Kumbh Melas on the same riverbanks, unless the issues are resolved. Margadarsaka Mandalam, a spiritual advisory body and collective of Hindu monks in Kerala, intervened to sort out differences but the initiative has not yielded results. A decade ago, in 2016, the efforts of Thirur Dinesh, a local journalist and a history enthusiast, led to the Mamankam festival being revived with religious fervour after decades. Since 2018, Swami Chidanandapuri, a vedanta scholar and founder of Advaithashramam in Kolathur, and Mata Amritanandamayi, who became the festival patron, have helped organise the event. Swami Chidananda Puri told TNM that the Margadaesakha Mandalam held multiple meetings with Anadavanam and the organising committee. “But we were not able to reach a positive conclusion," he said. items.title: Bengaluru police book Conrad Hotel Management after electrocution deaths
items.summary: The Halasuru police have registered a case against the management of Conrad Hotel in Bengaluru for alleged negligence following the deaths of two foreign nationals in a suspected electrocution incident at the hotel's swimming pool on October 30. The incident, which occurred at the swimming pool on the third floor of the five-star hotel, also left two others injured while attempting to rescue the victims. The deceased have been identified as Alexander Maximilian Theiss (57), a German national and crew member of Lufthansa Airlines, and Juraj Horvat (45), a Slovakian national working as a project manager with IBM. The injured persons have been identified as Mathew Desantis (41), an American national staying at the hotel, and Rahul Tiwari (28), a hotel employee working as a pool attendant and lifeguard. Both sustained injuries while attempting to rescue the victims and were shifted to Manipal Hospital for treatment. According to the complaint filed by Silvia Hotuatova (47), wife of Horvat, the couple had arrived in India on October 20 for a holiday and checked into Conrad Hotel on October 30. Horvat went swimming in the hotel's pool at around 5.15 pm when Silvia heard a loud noise from near the pool. On rushing to check, she found her husband motionless in the water. The complaint further stated that hotel staff members who attempted to rescue Horvat also sustained electric shocks. Another person subsequently alerted those present to the suspected presence of electric current in the pool, following which the hotel staff switched off the power supply. An American national, identified as Mathew Desantis, also attempted to rescue the victims and administer cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR). The victims were subsequently shifted to Manipal Hospital, where Horvat died while doctors attempted to revive him, while Theiss was declared brought dead. Manipal Hospitals, in a statement, said four people were brought to the hospital following the incident at around 5.10 pm on October 30. They included the German and Slovakian nationals, the American national and a 26-year-old hotel staff member. According to the hospital, the German national was brought dead, while the Slovakian national died despite resuscitation efforts. The hospital further stated that the American national had experienced a headache and was in a state of shock after attempting to rescue the victims. items.title: Apply for a Personal Loan – Eligibility and Steps
items.summary: When you approach any lender for a Personal Loan, they assess two main things – your creditworthiness and your capacity to repay the borrowed sums on time. To ascertain your creditworthiness, they ask you to fulfil certain conditions known as their eligibility criteria. If you fulfil these conditions, you can apply for the loan. Today, let’s learn about Personal Loan eligibility criteria and the methods to apply for Personal Loans online and offline. Personal Loan Eligibility Criteria Here are some general but crucial factors lenders consider while evaluating your Personal Loan application. · Your age: Lenders set minimum and maximum age limits based on your employment status – whether you are a salaried professional or a self-employed individual. As a salaried professional, you should be in the 18-60 years age group, but if you are self-employed, you should be between 23 and 65 years of age. Some lenders also take your retirement age and adjust loan repayment tenures accordingly. · Your income The monthly income you earn is another critical eligibility criterion lenders consider when you apply for Personal Loans. Your net (in-hand) monthly income, after the applicable tax deductions, should be at least ₹15,000 – ₹ 25,000, if you are a salaried employee (depending on your lender and area of residence). Self-employed individuals must show a minimum annual income of ₹300,000. · Your credit score Your credit score is the most critical parameter lenders consider while evaluating your Personal Loan application. This score is a 3-digit figure that gives your potential lender insight into how you handle debts. Most lenders require you to show a credit score of at least 700/750 points to be eligible for the loan. A lower score affects eligibility and may result in lenders charging higher interest rates. · Your duration of employment and stability Lenders also assess your duration of employment with the same firm. As a salaried applicant, you should ideally be employed with the same organisation for a minimum of 1 year. You should also be continuously employed for at least 2 years (even if you change jobs), with no long gaps in between. If you change jobs frequently, lenders take that into account while assessing your application. · Your FOIR and Debt-to-Income Ratio Lenders need to know if you have any existing debts.
